plain.text: A man named Ananias and his wife Sapphira sold some property. They kept back part of the money but brought the rest as if it were the full amount. Peter said, "Ananias, why has Satan filled your heart to lie to the Holy Spirit? The land was yours, and the money was at your disposal. You have not lied to people but to God." Ananias fell down and died. About three hours later, Sapphira came in, not knowing what had happened. She told the same lie, and she also fell down and died. Great fear seized the whole church and all who heard about it.

The apostles did many signs and wonders among the people. The believers met together in Solomon's Colonnade. More and more men and women believed in the Lord. People even carried the sick into the streets so that Peter's shadow might fall on them as he passed. Crowds came from towns around Jerusalem, bringing the sick and those tormented by evil spirits, and all were healed.

The high priest and his associates were filled with jealousy. They arrested the apostles and put them in the public jail. But during the night an angel of the Lord opened the prison doors and said, "Go, stand in the temple courts, and tell the people all about this new life." At daybreak they did. When officers went to the jail, they found it securely locked with guards at the doors, but no one inside.

The officials were puzzled. Then someone reported that the apostles were teaching in the temple. The captain brought them in, without force, fearing the people. The high priest said, "We gave you strict orders not to teach in this name." Peter and the apostles replied, "We must obey God rather than human beings!" They said God had raised Jesus, whom the leaders had killed, and exalted him as Prince and Saviour, to bring repentance and forgiveness. "We are witnesses of these things, and so is the Holy Spirit."

The council was furious and wanted to kill them. But Gamaliel, a respected Pharisee and teacher of the law, advised caution. Other movements had come to nothing when their leaders died. "If this plan is of human origin, it will fail. But if it is from God, you will not be able to stop them; you will only find yourselves fighting against God." They had the apostles flogged, ordered them not to speak in Jesus' name, and let them go. The apostles left rejoicing that they had been counted worthy of suffering disgrace for the Name. Day after day, in the temple and from house to house, they never stopped teaching that Jesus is the Messiah.

summary.bigIdea: God is at work in the early church: honesty matters deeply, and nothing can stop the message about Jesus.
points: Ananias and Sapphira lie to God and die, and the church is filled with awe.
An angel frees the apostles from prison, and they keep preaching.
"We must obey God rather than human beings!" Gamaliel warns against fighting God.
summary.reflection: The apostles rejoiced even when they suffered for Jesus. What do you think gave them that joy?
